second_order: Stretching maps and imagining how absurd layouts play
theme_note: Members collectively elaborate the extra-long-map joke by naming variants, requesting maps and servers, making maps, identifying their music, and imagining how the distorted layouts would play. What varies is whether they are spectators, requesters, players, or makers.

second_order: Baiting one another with April Fools tricks
theme_note: Members make, expose, and play along with fake updates, leaks, commands, reports, and reversals. The shared practice is trying to fool or knowingly extending the fooling; the object and the degree of belief vary.

second_order: Restyling the subreddit and staging April Fools events
theme_note: Members and moderators make April Fools into organized room or server activity through CSS proposals, gamedays, recurring threads, filters, Sentry/Sona styling, and the later banner. These differ from one-off bait because they temporarily organize a venue or recurring practice.

second_order: Celebrating and claiming the canvas work
theme_note: Members mark progress by saying they contributed, announcing completion or visibility, thanking builders, and circulating snapshots or timelapses. The claims range from individual pride to a collective 'we did it', and sometimes arrive before upkeep is actually over.

second_order: Building and revising shared TF2 canvas art
theme_note: Members turn proposals into pixels by choosing coordinates, supplying shapes and colours, adding text or figures, and repeatedly revising a workable design. The target shifts from a logo to lettering, Nopegineer, NOPE, and a centered redesign; participation ranges from calls and templates to reports of placed pixels.

second_order: Moving coordination through Discord, templates and scripts
theme_note: Members route design work through Discord, cross-posts, timing aids, templates, cooldown workarounds, and placement scripts. These tools can align work, but automation also produces an explicit fairness dispute between scripted maintenance and bare hands.

second_order: Negotiating borders and trading help with neighbours
theme_note: Members treat nearby drawings as parties to bargain with: they ask for room, respect or restore borders, offer mutual defence, request aid, and decide whether to help others. Relations vary between rivalry, conditional accommodation, apology, alliance, and refusal.

second_order: Asking the flood of place posts to make room
theme_note: Members object to r/place filling r/tf2 and propose megathreads, filters, removal, or a separate subreddit. Some simply ask what the flood means; others call it spam or pointless, so the strength of rejection varies.

Small exchanges correct a bot, spelling, grammar, or phrasing and then turn the correction into teasing, insult, or wordplay. These codes do not join the event practices merely because they occur beside them, so they remain a small practice of their own.

second_order: Arguing over expansion and what belongs in the design
theme_note: Members contest the extent and identity of the shared area: the long neck, neighbouring Valve symbols, logo redesigns, outlines, and text are accepted, reversed, or redirected. What varies is the preferred object, but the common practice is deciding which change counts as improvement rather than intrusion.

second_order: Maintaining and repairing the TF2 area
theme_note: Members recruit routine attention to clean, fix, defend, and keep recognizable art that already exists. Some calls answer vandalism or mistaken redesigns, while others report ordinary pixel correction; this is upkeep rather than proposing a new motif.

second_order: Rallying against the void and rebuilding NOPE
theme_note: A concentrated attack turns posts into alarms, reinforcements, status reports, repair calls, and restoration claims. Participants vary between defending, mourning, and declaring recovery, but all orient to the loss and rebuilding of the same canvas work.

second_order: Ending the event and making a shared memory
theme_note: After placement closes, members congratulate one another, recount defence, mourn lost neighbours and motifs, preserve timelapses, and debate what the imperfect final canvas means. Celebration, criticism, thanks, and memorializing all make the finished event into a retrospective account.

second_order: Reusing canvas art as sprays, flairs and icons
theme_note: Members crop, restore, separate, resize, and request the finished designs for Steam pictures, sprays, subreddit flair, a mobile Snoo, and a possible subreddit logo. Requests, production, correction, and approval vary, but each carries canvas imagery into a new use.
